met_analysis:
The Low Pressure Area over Southwest Madhya Pradesh & neighbourhood lies over Southeast Rajasthan and adjoining Gujarat Region & Southwest Madhya Pradesh at 0530 hrs IST of today, the 14th September 2026.
The associated cyclonic circulation extending upto 5.8 km above mean sea level tilting southwestwards with height. It is likely to move west-northwestwards across South Rajasthan & North Gujarat during next 24 hours.
The Monsoon trough at mean sea level now passes through Deesha, centre of Low Pressure Area over Southeast Rajasthan and adjoining Gujarat Region & Southwest Madhya Pradesh, Bhopal, Jabalpur, Daltonganj, Digha and thence southeastwards to Northeast Bay of Bengal.
The trough now runs from Eastcentral Arabian Sea to Bihar across Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, north Chhattisgarh & Jharkhand and extends upto 4.5 km above mean sea level.
A trough runs from the cyclonic circulation associated with the Low Pressure area over Southeast Rajasthan and adjoining Gujarat Region & Southwest Madhya Pradesh to Westcentral Bay of Bengal across Southwest Madhya Pradesh, Vidarbha, Telangana, South Coastal Andhra Pradesh at 4.5 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Coastal Andhra Pradesh & neighbourhood persists and now seen at 5.8 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation south Tamil Nadu coast & neighbourhood at 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over south Konkan adjoining Eastcentral Arabian sea at 7.6 km above mean sea level has merged with the cyclonic circulation associated with the Low Pressure area over Southeast Rajasthan and adjoining Gujarat Region & Southwest Madhya Pradesh.
The Western Disturbance as a trough in middle tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level now runs roughly along Long. 75°E to the north of Lat. 30°N.
An upper air cyclonic circulation lies over Northwest Bay of Bengal & neighbourhood between 1.5 & 3.1 km above mean sea level.
